title: the Glass Steppe Rising Revisited
premise: Paloma Reyes, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has never left the valley where magic cannot follow — until a stranger named Ilya arrives carrying a prophecy book written a century ago that names tonight's date and his own death. The covenant binding the Glass Steppe to the mortal realms is breaking, and the dead Paloma hears are its forgotten signatories demanding she reforge it before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Crossing into the Steppe strips away her valley-born protections and forces her to confront the inheritance of blood-magic her family fled generations ago. In the end, Paloma rewrites the covenant with her own carved bone instead of the old sacrificial law, saving Ilya but choosing exile from the valley forever.
about_author: B. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former mortuary archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed remains in the high desert. Their fiction blends folk necromancy, quiet grief, and landscapes that remember more than the living do.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses Magic
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She carves a memorial bone for a drowned child while hearing the dead murmur at the valley's edge. Establishes her craft, her isolation, and the rule: magic cannot follow past the boundary stones. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Boundary
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Ilya stumbles through the stones bleeding light instead of blood, clutching an ancient book. He speaks her name before she gives it. Emotional beat: wary fascination; the first crack in her sealed life.

chapters.title: The Book That Names Tonight
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The prophecy book, written a century prior, records this exact date, Ilya's arrival, and a line about 'the carver who hears.' He confesses he was sent by a dying order. Emotional beat: dread of being a character rather than a person.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She consults the valley's honored dead, who go silent when asked about the covenant — a silence they've kept for a hundred years. Her grandmother's ghost leaves one word: 'Steppe.' Emotional beat: betrayal by the very dead she serves.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. He explains the moon's thirteenth turn: when the covenant lapses, the Glass Steppe floods into the mortal world, and everything magic touches unravels. The valley's protection will not hold. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership forged under a deadline.

chapters.title: The Carver's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Searching her grandmother's chest, she finds a half-finished bone sigil matching the book's diagrams — proof her family were original covenant-smiths who fled their duty. Emotional beat: anger at inherited lies.

chapters.title: Crossing the Stones
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They cross together; magic rushes back into Paloma like cold water, and the dead of the Steppe become deafening. The valley shrinks behind them. Emotional beat: vertigo of becoming someone new.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. A plain of fused glass stretching to a broken horizon, mirages of cities trapped inside it. He teaches Paloma the order's signs. Emotional beat: awe curdling into homesickness for a place neither can return to yet.

chapters.title: Voices in the Glass
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The dead here don't whisper — they argue. Factions of signatory ghosts demand different terms of renewal. One claims her grandmother's name. Emotional beat: overwhelmed but needed, perhaps for the first time.

chapters.title: The Order of the Last Page
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Flashback chapters within his memory: how the order found him, why he was chosen as messenger, and what happened to the last messenger — whose bones Paloma now carries unknowingly. Emotional beat: guilt revealed.

chapters.title: The Salt Court
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They reach a court of salt pillars ruled by Vess, a signatory ghost-queen who offers shelter and poisoned hospitality. Vess wants the covenant rewritten in her faction's favor. Emotional beat: learning that allies can be predators.

chapters.title: Terms and Thorns
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Negotiation scene; Vess reveals the covenant's original price — a living smith bound into the glass each century. Paloma realizes why her ancestors ran. Emotional beat: horror of the family secret confirmed.

chapters.title: Night of the First Turn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. First moon-turn marker passes; the Steppe shudders, and a city-mirage briefly becomes real, screaming. They barely escape. Emotional beat: the deadline made flesh.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sings
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her carving resonates with the Steppe itself — she discovers her craft works on the land, not just the dead. Hope kindles. Emotional beat: first taste of agency.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Hollow Wind
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The order's rival, the Hollow Wind, sends hunters to kill the messenger and let the covenant die. Chase across glass dunes. Emotional beat: fear sharpening loyalty into something warmer.

chapters.title: Campfire Confessions
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Quiet interlude: Ilya admits he volunteered because he was dying anyway; Paloma admits she never wanted to leave the valley — or to be alone in it. Emotional beat: intimacy earned through honesty.

chapters.title: The Second Turn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Another marker passes; the boundary stones behind them crumble on the horizon. No retreat now. Emotional beat: grief for the door closing.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Vess returns offering an army if Paloma agrees to bind Ilya as the new sacrifice — the book's literal reading. Paloma refuses; war follows them out. Emotional beat: defiance with a cost.

chapters.title: The Mirrored Ford
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A river of reflections where each sees alternate lives: Paloma as a valley mother, Ilya as a healthy scholar. Temptation scene. Emotional beat: mourning the selves they cannot be.

chapters.title: The Dead Signatories
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. They find the council-chasm where the original thirteen signatories sleep in glass. Waking them requires a voice the dead trust — Paloma's. Emotional beat: weight of being chosen.

chapters.title: Thirteen Ghosts, One Question
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The council wakes and asks the covenant's founding question anew: what is survival worth? Each ghost gives a different answer drawn from their death. Emotional beat: philosophical pivot of the novel.

chapters.title: The Third Turn and the Treachery
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. A hunter infiltrates their camp; the prophecy book is stolen. Without it, no one knows the rite's full wording. Emotional beat: despair and self-blame.

chapters.title: Chasing the Book Through Bone Country
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Pursuit into a canyon of fossil giants where the Hollow Wind nests. She negotiates passage using her grandmother's sigil. Emotional beat: cunning replacing helplessness.

chapters.title: The Hollow Wind Speaks
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The antagonist — a former signatory who faked her death to escape the sacrifice — argues annihilation is mercy. Her logic lands hard. Emotional beat: doubt that nearly wins.

chapters.title: Half a Rite
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They recover the torn final page; the rest was destroyed a century ago by Paloma's grandmother. The family didn't just flee — they sabotaged the covenant. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A hidden letter in the sigil explains: her grandmother refused to bind another child and broke the rite deliberately, buying the valley a hundred years. Emotional beat: forgiveness across generations.

chapters.title: The Fifth Turn
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Time compresses; turns now pass in days. The Steppe begins leaking into the mortal world — rain falls upward over the valley. Emotional beat: urgency without panic, commitment without certainty.

chapters.title: Allies of Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Vess, humbled by the Hollow Wind's rising, offers truce. Uneasy alliance formed around Paloma's alternative plan: carve a new covenant from willing bone, not bound flesh. Emotional beat: coalition-building against odds.

chapters.title: The Carving Begins
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Montage of craft: she carves the covenant-bone from her own healed fractures and the last messenger's remains, each ghost contributing a clause. Emotional beat: creation as collaboration with the dead.

chapters.title: What Ilya Hid
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Revealed: the prophecy names him dying at the rite regardless. He hid it to keep Paloma moving. Confrontation. Emotional beat: love tested by protective lies.

chapters.title: The Ninth Turn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She chooses to keep going anyway — not to save the world first, but because she refuses a story written by anyone else. Emotional beat: fierce self-authorship.

chapters.title: March on the Chasm
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The allied host marches; the Hollow Wind's storm meets them at the council-chasm. Battle joined among sleeping signatories. Emotional beat: courage amid chaos.

chapters.title: The Storm Breaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Mid-battle, the Hollow Wind confronts Paloma directly, offering to spare everyone if she simply walks away — the valley's old temptation. Emotional beat: the theme weaponized.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. One turn remains. The rite must begin at moonrise. Wounded, outnumbered, they descend into the chasm while the sky splits. Emotional beat: calm at the edge of ruin.

chapters.title: The Rite of Willing Bone
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Climax part one: Paloma performs the rewritten covenant, every ghost signing in voice, Vess holding the line above. The old law fights back through the glass itself. Emotional beat: transcendence through craft.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Climax part two: the covenant demands its anchor. Ilya steps forward to die as prophesied — but Paloma has carved herself into the bone too, splitting the price between two willing souls. Emotional beat: sacrifice subverted by shared burden.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The moon completes its turn; the covenant holds, remade on consent instead of coercion. The Hollow Wind dissolves, finally allowed to rest. The Steppe goes quiet — truly quiet. Emotional beat: release after unbearable tension.

chapters.title: Aftermath at the Stones
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They return to the boundary; the valley's protection is gone, replaced by the new covenant's gentler terms. Paloma can never again be the woman who stayed. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Hears
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Epilogue-in-motion: Ilya, alive but bound to the Steppe's rhythms, asks what comes next. Paloma answers by beginning a new commission — carving names for the newly peaceful dead. Emotional beat: hope as daily practice.

chapters.title: Rising, Revisited
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Final chapter: a year later, travelers cross open stones freely; the dead speak in daylight and are answered. Paloma teaches an apprentice with her grandmother's tools, the prophecy book closed at last. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from burden to gift.
